matches.quote: The edge peak sits at E_F, only ~10 meV above the reported VBM (−10 meV). It is therefore at the very bottom edge of the gap
Only one dI/dV map at +7 mV is shown... Maps at several energies inside the gap and at the band edges... are needed.
The "V-shaped dip between ±50 mV" (or ±10 mV) in the island-center spectrum is itself unexplained, since the bulk gap is ~300 meV wide.
No trivial-phase control. The authors' own Si₂Te₂/Sb₂Te₃ system (trivial) is the ideal reference: edges there should be measured with identical parameters
The islands are small (~8–10 nm across, Fig. 5a,d). With a 2–3 nm decay length on each side, the edge states would occupy a large fraction of the island
if HfTe₂ states lie inside the Si₂Te₂ gap, the heterostructure is globally metallic... helical edge states can hybridize with the substrate continuum.
"Independent of step geometry" is not established. There is no systematic comparison of edge orientations (zigzag vs. armchair-like) or terminations, and no assessment of edges adjacent to defects
No probe of helicity. There are no QPI or backscattering-suppression measurements near the edge, no magnetic-field or spin-polarized STM tests of helicity
The "V-shaped dip between ±50 mV" (or ±10 mV) in the island-center spectrum is itself unexplained, since the bulk gap is ~300 meV wide.
The ring is inhomogeneous, and the missing segment on the lower edge is attributed to "tip effects" without evidence.
The Z₂ calculation via Wannier charge centers for a metallic heterostructure requires a clearly specified set of occupied bands, isolated by a direct gap at every k-point.
The robustness of the band inversion against functional choice and interlayer distance should also be reported.
With a 2–3 nm decay length on each side, the edge states would occupy a large fraction of the island and could hybridize across it, opening a finite-size gap.
A linearly dispersing 1D helical edge mode has an approximately constant (Van Hove-free) LDOS across the entire bulk gap... The authors must explain quantitatively why a peak... is expected
At such an energy, the peak can easily arise from trivial causes: edge-induced upward band bending of the valence band; shifted valence-band states localized at under-coordinated edge atoms

notes: C5 and C6 come from the same small-island geometry (~8-10 nm island vs 2-3 nm edge state); P18 directly raises C6 (hybridization opening an edge gap) and partly raises C5 (small island size + quantum confinement requiring larger islands, while P1 asks for gap statistics across the 20 islands), without explicitly stating that edge-state bleed-in and tip convolution obstruct the bulk gap measurement. C16 critiques an SM claim about non-linear dispersion causing the edge peak; without the SM, P23 raises the exact main-text paradox (1D linear Dirac dispersion gives a Van Hove-free plateau rather than a narrow peak). C19 (WCC parameter convergence) and C20 (coexistence of edge and bulk states in SI nanoribbon bands) are judged 'partly' because P8 and P6 raise the closely corresponding issues on the main-text WCC specification and substrate-continuum overlap.
